idiom_name: coroutineScope + async/awaitAll on Dispatchers.Default (Channel fan-out for a fixed pool)
implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies the whole structure: coroutineScope bounds the master's lifetime, async starts one child coroutine per subtask on Dispatchers.Default (a shared pool sized to the available cores), and awaitAll is the aggregation point, while a failure cancels the remaining children through structured concurrency instead of leaving orphaned workers. For a persistent worker set, N coroutines ranging over a Channel fan out the work (the documented fan-out idiom) and limitedParallelism pins a dispatcher to a fixed worker count; the classic master object is only justified when the worker set must outlive the call.
pitfalls: Dispatchers.Default is a shared CPU pool, not a thread pin: blocking calls inside the block occupy its threads - use Dispatchers.IO or limitedParallelism for blocking work.
An exception in one child cancels the siblings, so partial results are discarded unless the scope is supervised (supervisorScope) or each child handles its own failure.
awaitAll launches one coroutine per element; for unbounded streams this needs a Channel plus a fixed worker set, or the pool degenerates into coroutine-per-task.
